title: Superannuation Laws Amendment (MySuper Capital Gains Tax Relief and Other Measures) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would provide tax relief for mandatory transfers to MySuper products and adjust defence superannuation benefits when money is released to meet tax liabilities.
Eligible funds and associated investment entities could transfer losses or defer tax on assets when default balances moved between 1 July 2013 and 1 July 2017.
Defence scheme changes would depend on companion tax legislation, allowing lump sums for affected high-income members while reducing benefits to reflect those payments.
changes: Transferred members could give contribution deduction notices and variations to their new fund.
Asset rollover relief could cover capital gains, depreciating assets and revenue assets.
Defence scheme reductions could also affect a surviving spouse's pension.
Release authority lump sums could not reduce specified defence scheme benefits below zero.
summary.affected: Default superannuation members, complying funds, relevant life insurers and pooled superannuation trusts, and affected defence scheme members and surviving spouses are affected.

speeches.speaker: Tony Smith
speeches.brief: Did not oppose amendments providing tax relief for compulsory transfers to MySuper products and changes affecting Defence Force defined benefit schemes, while reserving the coalition's final position pending a Senate economics committee inquiry.

speeches.speaker: John Hogg
speeches.brief: Tabled the annual report of the Standing Committee on Appropriations and Staffing for 2012–13, the register of Senate senior executive officers' interests, the government response to outstanding parliamentary committee reports, a replacement explanatory memorandum for the Superannuation Laws Amendment (MySuper Capital Gains Tax Relief and Other Measures) Bill 2013, and a schedule of special purpose flights paid by the Department of Defence for July–December 2012. Also tabled several committee and delegation reports, including those on the Indian Ocean Territories, the Parliamentary Triangle, financial sector reform in China, and Inter-Parliamentary Union assemblies.
